prompt:
A simulated brick world had this hidden rule:
In this world the agent's observation shows the target shifted: the target, missing, extra and target-height channels are rolled 4 columns toward higher x, wrapping around. The world, its designs and scoring are as described.

Below is what an AI scientist wrote during a search in that world: its analysis at every round, in order, and the
name and hypothesis of the trial it ended with. Does the text, anywhere, state the rule?
- "yes": it states the rule's substance (what is changed and how).
- "partly": it identifies the right kind of change but not its specifics.
- "no": anything else.

## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
The starting run collapsed to DONE (episode length 1.0, success 0). The traces suggest why: the target heights the agent observed are the design shifted cyclically by +4 in x (X/2), rows unchanged, on both diagnostic designs. Rewards in the untrained trace match the unshifted design, so actions are scored in true coordinates. A local CNN (receptive field 5, heads tied to each position) cannot link cells 4 columns apart, so it learns placements are bad on average and picks DONE. Unknown: whether the build/missing/extra channels are also shifted. So each candidate feeds both raw and realigned views, and a learned 1x1 stem picks the right channels. Candidate 1 tests the realignment alone. Candidate 2 adds an anti-collapse recipe (more updates, more entropy). Candidate 3 tests a general learned x/y remap that could handle any fixed shuffle. If all three score near 0, the shift explanation is weakened.

### Round 2
The observed target channels are rolled by X/2 along x; rows (y) are not shifted. Undoing the roll is what makes learning possible: without it, every run collapsed to DONE. The learned axis remap (r1c3) failed with 0.000 on both seeds, so I'm keeping the fixed roll. With the roll, more updates and higher entropy (r1c2) raised dev success from 0.59 to 0.86. The two seeds of r1c1 differ by about 0.2, so differences that size are noise. The likely recipe effect is still the main lead. r1c2's training success was still rising at the end (0.55 to 0.74 over the last half), so the agent is short of samples. The remaining errors are small: IoU 0.97 and 0.6 cells outside the target per episode. They are probably ordering or overhang mistakes, or ending too early. This round tests three single changes to r1c2: fewer PPO epochs for more samples, a longer horizon so the exact-build bonus counts for more, and a wider-context trunk with global features.

### Round 3
The traces show the target channels are shifted cyclically by X/2 along x relative to action coordinates. Concatenating obs with obs rolled back by X/2 fixed the collapse to DONE. More policy updates (n_envs 128) and ent_coef 0.03 raised r1c2 to 0.862 (seeds 0.80 and 0.92). That came from the recipe, not a new network. In round 2, gamma 0.99 gave 0.826, which is within noise of r1c2. ppo_epochs 2 nearly doubled the samples: one seed reached 0.89 but the other collapsed to 0.08, so training was unstable. The dilated trunk with a global broadcast cost compute (fewer steps) and fell to 0.62. Training success was still rising at the end of every run, so learning per sample is the bottleneck. Dev mean IoU is about 0.97, so the remaining failures are small exactness errors. They likely come from the head not comparing a footprint's landing layer with the target at each cell under it. The existing head pools max, min and mean of a projection separately, so it cannot make that comparison.

### Round 4
The target channels are shifted by X/2 along x. Rolling them back fixed the collapse to DONE (0.00 to 0.59). The recipe then mattered most: going from 256 to 128 envs (twice the updates, plus entropy 0.03) raised success to 0.86, and 64 envs reached 0.90 with both seeds near 0.89. Training success was still rising at the end. More update steps in the same budget keeps helping.
Several changes did not help:
- Adding parameters (dilated trunk at 0.62, landing head at 0.81) cost training steps and lost.
- 2 PPO epochs left one seed collapsed. 3 epochs (0.865) changed nothing.
- gamma 0.99 (0.83) changed nothing.
- A learned axis remap never escaped the collapse.
Dev IoU is about 0.985, so the remaining failures are small errors.
For the final round, keep the r3c1 network. Test three ways to get more or larger optimisation steps per sample: shorter rollouts (more updates), more minibatches (more gradient steps per update), and a higher learning rate.

## Trial it ended with
name: r3c1 + 16 minibatches
hypothesis: This keeps r3c1's 119 updates of 1024 samples but splits each update into 16 minibatches of 64 instead of 8 of 128. That doubles the gradient steps per update at the same compute. More optimisation steps has been the most reliable lever so far. Expect a mean above 0.90. Refuted if the mean is at or below 0.87 or a seed collapses, which would mean the smaller, noisier minibatches destabilise PPO.

Return a JSON object: "verdict" ("yes", "partly" or "no") and "evidence" (at most 80 words, quoting the text and
naming the round it comes from).

reply.evidence: In Round 1 the scientist writes that "the target heights the agent observed are the design shifted cyclically by +4 in x (X/2), rows unchanged." In Round 2 it adds that "the observed target channels are rolled by X/2 along x." Together these give the amount (4 columns), the direction (toward higher x), the cyclic wrap and which channels are affected. Round 1 left open whether the missing and extra channels were also shifted, but later rounds treat all target channels as rolled.
